claim: Joseph proposes administrative action; Pharaoh appoints him over his house/land, and the text states Joseph is thirty years old when he stands before Pharaoh.
label: Joseph is appointed over Egypt

claim: Joseph recognizes his brothers while they do not recognize him; he tests them and has Simeon bound before their eyes.
label: Joseph recognizes his brothers

claim: Judah guarantees Benjamin's return to Jacob and later pleads to remain as a servant instead of Benjamin.
label: Judah's guarantee and self-offer

claim: Joseph reveals himself to his brothers and tells them that God sent him ahead to preserve life.
label: Joseph reveals himself and interprets the past

claim: The Hebrew midwives fear God and do not do what the king of Egypt commands concerning the male children; God deals well with them.
label: Midwives fear God

claim: Pharaoh commands his people to cast every newborn Hebrew son into the river while letting daughters live.
label: Pharaoh's river command

claim: A Levite woman hides her son, places him in a basket among the reeds, Pharaoh's daughter finds him, and later names him Moses because she drew him out of the water.
label: Moses' birth, basket, rescue, and naming

claim: Moses sees an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, kills the Egyptian, and later flees from Pharaoh to Midian.
label: Moses kills an Egyptian and flees

claim: God hears Israel's groaning, remembers his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, sees the children of Israel, and knows.
label: God hears and remembers covenant

claim: At Horeb, God calls to Moses from the bush, declares the ground holy, commissions him to Pharaoh, and identifies himself with the divine name and the God of the patriarchs.
label: Burning bush, holy ground, commission, and divine name

claim: Israel is instructed to take a lamb, apply blood to the doorposts and lintel, eat in readiness, and the blood is described as a sign when judgment passes through Egypt.
label: Passover lamb and blood sign

claim: The day is commanded as a memorial, and seven days of unleavened bread are prescribed.
label: Memorial and unleavened bread

claim: At midnight the firstborn in Egypt are struck; Pharaoh tells Moses and Aaron to leave with Israel, and Egyptians urge the people out.
label: Death of firstborn and departure pressure

claim: The passage states that the dwelling/stay of the children of Israel was four hundred thirty years and marks the departure after that period.
label: The text states four hundred thirty years

claim: God does not lead Israel by the nearest Philistine route; Moses carries Joseph's bones; Yahweh goes before them in cloud by day and fire by night.
label: Route, Joseph's bones, cloud and fire

claim: Israel fears at the sea; Moses speaks of Yahweh's deliverance; the sea divides, Israel crosses on dry ground, Egyptians are overwhelmed, and Israel sees Yahweh's saving action.
label: Sea crossing and deliverance

claim: Yahweh tells Moses that if Israel obeys his voice and keeps his covenant, they will be his special possession among the peoples, a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation.
label: Covenant proposal: treasured possession and priestly kingdom

claim: Moses places Yahweh's words before the elders, and the people answer together that they will do all Yahweh has spoken.
label: People accept the covenant words

claim: The people are consecrated, boundaries are set around the mountain, and Moses repeatedly mediates instructions as Yahweh descends on Sinai.
label: Preparation and mountain boundaries

claim: God speaks the commandments concerning exclusive worship, idols, the divine name, and Sabbath rest.
label: First commandments and Sabbath
